A premature timeout forces the congestion window back to 1 (slow start), drastically tanking overall throughput even if the link has no physical packet loss.
questions.hint: Look closely at the interaction between high propagation delay, timer estimation algorithms, and how congestion control states reset.
questions.relatedConcept: TCP Spurious Timeouts and RTO Estimation
questions.interviewTip: This distinguishes candidates who understand deep transport-layer congestion and timing mechanics from those who only know basic TCP flags and handshake steps.

questions.question: [Computer Networks • Test 1 • Q15] What happens when a network interface card (NIC) configured with an MTU of 1500 bytes receives an incoming Ethernet frame containing an IPv4 packet whose Total Length field is specified as 1510 bytes, assuming the frame passes standard FCS validation?
options: The packet is automatically fragmented into two fragments before being passed to the transport layer.
The NIC truncates the payload down to 1500 bytes and delivers the truncated packet to the OS kernel.
The receiving host sends an ICMP Source Quench message back to the sender to adjust its MSS.
The NIC or IP layer drops the packet as a giant/oversized frame or malformed datagram.
questions.correctAnswer: The NIC or IP layer drops the packet as a giant/oversized frame or malformed datagram.
questions.explanation: If a frame/packet exceeds the interface's Maximum Transmission Unit (MTU) upon reception and fragmentation cannot be performed locally (or if it arrives as a single layer-2 frame larger than MTU minus headers, or if the IPv4 header Total Length exceeds the actual payload or interface limits without valid fragmentation bits permitting it), the packet is treated as a jumbo or oversized frame and discarded by the data link or network layer.
questions.hint: Think about what happens to incoming packets that violate the local link MTU constraints without valid fragment offsets.
questions.relatedConcept: MTU enforcement and handling of oversized incoming network frames
questions.interviewTip: Interviewers use this to see if candidates understand packet reception limits versus transmission-side fragmentation.

questions.question: [Computer Networks • Test 1 • Q16] In the context of the Border Gateway Protocol (BGP), what is the primary consequence if a router's configured Hold Time timer expires before receiving either an update or a keepalive message from its peer?
options: The router tears down the BGP peering session, transitions the state to Idle, and initiates route withdrawal procedures for paths learned from that peer.
The router temporarily drops the TCP connection but keeps the BGP peering state machine in the OpenConfirm state for up to 4 minutes.
The router increments the BGP dampening penalty points on all prefixes advertised by that peer by a factor of two.
The router downgrades the BGP session from version 4 to version 3 to negotiate more lenient timeout intervals.
questions.correctAnswer: The router tears down the BGP peering session, transitions the state to Idle, and initiates route withdrawal procedures for paths learned from that peer.
questions.explanation: The BGP Hold Timer dictates the maximum time a router waits between successive KEEPALIVE or UPDATE messages. If it expires, the peer is considered dead, the TCP connection is closed, the BGP state resets to Idle, and all routes learned from that peer are withdrawn or invalidated.
questions.hint: Consider the lifecycle of a BGP peering session when keepalives stop arriving.
questions.relatedConcept: BGP Keepalive and Hold Timer expiration behavior
questions.interviewTip: This tests core routing protocol failure recovery mechanisms expected in network engineering and reliability roles.

questions.question: [Computer Networks • Test 1 • Q17] What is the primary mechanism by which HTTP/2 achieves multiplexing over a single TCP connection, thereby solving head-of-line blocking at the application layer?
options: Establishing multiple parallel underlying TCP sub-connections using SCTP protocol encapsulation
Dividing requests and responses into independent, interleaved binary-encoded frames associated with specific streams
Using dynamic Huffman coding to compress HTTP header fields so small control packets bypass congestion windows
Requiring the client to queue subsequent requests until a full window acknowledgment is received from the server
questions.correctAnswer: Dividing requests and responses into independent, interleaved binary-encoded frames associated with specific streams
questions.explanation: HTTP/2 introduces a binary framing layer that breaks down HTTP communication into independent messages called frames. These frames can be interleaved and sent concurrently over a single TCP connection, identified by a stream identifier, eliminating application-layer head-of-line blocking.
questions.hint: Think about how data is split and structured at the transport-adjacent layer inside HTTP/2.
questions.relatedConcept: HTTP/2 Multiplexing and Framing
questions.interviewTip: Interviewers ask this to test your understanding of how protocol layers interact—specifically how HTTP/2 attempts to solve TCP-level single-stream constraints via framing.

questions.question: [Computer Networks • Test 1 • Q18] In the DiffServ (Differentiated Services) QoS architecture, how does the Explicit Congestion Notification (ECN) mechanism signal network congestion to end hosts without dropping packets?
options: Intermediate switches flood the destination with low-priority ICMP Source Quench control messages
The sending host periodically transmits out-of-band probe packets that bypass router queue buffers
Routers set specific bit patterns in the IP header (DSCP/ToS field) which are echoed back by the receiver via transport layer acknowledgments
Routers forcefully terminate TCP sessions prematurely if buffer utilization crosses the high-water mark
questions.correctAnswer: Routers set specific bit patterns in the IP header (DSCP/ToS field) which are echoed back by the receiver via transport layer acknowledgments
questions.explanation: ECN allows end-to-end notification of network congestion without dropping packets. Routers mark the ECN bits in the IP header of qualifying packets when queues exceed a threshold; the receiving transport layer (e.g., TCP) then echoes this congestion signal back to the sender, which reduces its congestion window.
questions.hint: Look at how IP header fields interact with transport layer acknowledgments during congestion.
questions.relatedConcept: Explicit Congestion Notification (ECN) and DiffServ
questions.interviewTip: Crucial for systems and network engineering roles involving high-throughput data centers where packet drops cause unnecessary retransmissions.

questions.question: [Computer Networks • Test 1 • Q19] What happens when an Ethernet interface receives an incoming frame that is smaller than the minimum 64-byte IEEE 802.3 frame size specification?
options: The receiving NIC automatically pads the frame with trailing zero bytes up to 64 bytes and passes it up to the operating system stack.
The receiving NIC forwards the frame directly to the upper-layer network protocol, which handles the padding internally.
The local switch intercepts the undersized frame, buffers it, requests retransmission from the sender, and logs a collision.
The receiving network interface card (NIC) drops the frame as a runt frame and typically increments its alignment or runt error counters.
questions.correctAnswer: The receiving network interface card (NIC) drops the frame as a runt frame and typically increments its alignment or runt error counters.
questions.explanation: Ethernet requires a minimum frame size of 64 bytes (header + payload + FCS) to ensure proper collision detection in shared CSMA/CD environments. Frames smaller than this are classified as 'runt frames' caused by collisions or faulty hardware and are discarded immediately by the receiving hardware interface rather than being padded.
questions.hint: Consider what happens to frames that do not meet the minimum physical transmission constraints required for collision detection.
questions.relatedConcept: Ethernet framing, runt frames, and collision detection constraints
questions.interviewTip: Interviewers use this to test your understanding of physical layer and data link layer constraints, moving beyond basic IP routing into how raw hardware handles malformed frames.

questions.question: [Computer Networks • Test 1 • Q20] In standard socket programming, what is the precise operational significance of calling 'shutdown(sockfd, SHUT_WR)' compared to calling 'close(sockfd)'?
options: shutdown with SHUT_WR sends a FIN packet to gracefully close the output direction while leaving the input stream open to receive remaining data, whereas close immediately destroys the socket descriptor and releases all associated resources.
shutdown with SHUT_WR terminates both read and write channels like close, but prevents the operating system from sending a TCP RST packet upon termination.
shutdown with SHUT_WR flushes the socket output buffer to the network card but keeps the application-level file descriptor active for writing new data later.
shutdown with SHUT_WR is an asynchronous call that queues a half-close operation, whereas close is a blocking system call that waits for the final ACK of the FIN.
questions.correctAnswer: shutdown with SHUT_WR sends a FIN packet to gracefully close the output direction while leaving the input stream open to receive remaining data, whereas close immediately destroys the socket descriptor and releases all associated resources.
questions.explanation: The shutdown function with SHUT_WR allows a TCP endpoint to signal that it has finished sending data (initiating the connection tear-down by sending a FIN) while still remaining capable of reading any incoming data sent by the peer until the peer also closes its end. A standard close call tears down both directions simultaneously and destroys the file descriptor.
questions.hint: Think about TCP half-close mechanics and how applications communicate that they are done transmitting without losing incoming data.
questions.relatedConcept: Socket API shutdown semantics vs close mechanics
questions.interviewTip: This question assesses deep systems networking knowledge, distinguishing between raw file descriptor lifecycle management and nuanced TCP protocol state transitions.

questions.question: [Computer Networks • Test 1 • Q21] What is the primary architectural advantage of HTTP/2 server push over traditional HTTP/1.1 asset fetching when a client requests an HTML document containing stylesheet and script references?
options: It completely bypasses browser cache validation rules for all pushed assets, guaranteeing fresh execution.
It eliminates the initial round-trip delay required for the client to parse the HTML and discover subsequent dependent resources.
It compresses the TCP handshake phase by pre-allocating stream windows before the client establishes a connection.
It enables multi-tenant resource sharing across independent domain origins without requiring CORS preflight checks.
questions.correctAnswer: It eliminates the initial round-trip delay required for the client to parse the HTML and discover subsequent dependent resources.
questions.explanation: In HTTP/1.1, a browser must fetch the HTML, parse it, and then discover and request linked stylesheets or scripts sequentially, incurring multiple round-trip times (RTTs). HTTP/2 server push allows the server to proactively send these resources to the client cache alongside the HTML before the client even requests them, eliminating the discovery delay.
questions.hint: Think about what phase of the page-loading lifecycle is avoided regarding asset discovery.
questions.relatedConcept: HTTP/2 Server Push vs HTTP/1.1 Resource Discovery Latency
questions.interviewTip: Interviewers use this to test your understanding of web protocol performance optimizations and the elimination of network round-trips.

questions.question: [Computer Networks • Test 1 • Q22] How does the QUIC transport protocol mitigate head-of-line (HoL) blocking compared to HTTP/2 running over standard TCP?
options: QUIC forces all streams to share a single congestion window but dynamically reprioritizes packets based on application-layer headers.
QUIC avoids packet loss entirely by employing aggressive forward error correction (FEC) at the physical layer instead of retransmissions.
QUIC implements independent stream-level flow control and multiplexing directly over UDP, ensuring a packet loss on one stream does not stall delivery on other streams.
QUIC replaces packet acknowledgments with continuous stream polling, removing sequential delivery constraints at the transport layer.
questions.correctAnswer: QUIC implements independent stream-level flow control and multiplexing directly over UDP, ensuring a packet loss on one stream does not stall delivery on other streams.
questions.explanation: While HTTP/2 multiplexes multiple streams over a single TCP connection, a single TCP packet loss causes transport-layer head-of-line blocking for the entire connection, stalling all streams. QUIC runs over UDP and natively implements independent streams; a lost packet on one stream only impacts that specific stream.
questions.hint: Consider the difference between transport-layer multiplexing (TCP) and application-aware stream handling over datagrams.
questions.relatedConcept: QUIC Transport Layer Multiplexing and Stream-Level HoL Blocking Mitigation
questions.interviewTip: Crucial for modern transport protocols; tests whether candidates understand why moving from TCP to UDP-based reliable transport solves TCP's fundamental transport bottleneck.

questions.question: [Computer Networks • Test 1 • Q23] What is the primary operational consequence when DNS EDNS0 (Extension Mechanisms for DNS) is not supported or is heavily filtered along the path between a validating resolver and an authoritative nameserver?
options: The resolver automatically switches from UDP port 53 to port 443 to bypass middlebox inspection.
The authoritative server responds with an immediate HTTP 406 Not Acceptable status code.
All authoritative nameservers for the zone are permanently blacklisted by public root hints.
The resolver falls back to TCP or truncates responses, potentially leading to SERVFAIL or timeouts when handling large DNSSEC-signed responses.
questions.correctAnswer: The resolver falls back to TCP or truncates responses, potentially leading to SERVFAIL or timeouts when handling large DNSSEC-signed responses.
questions.explanation: EDNS0 allows DNS UDP payload sizes to exceed the traditional 512-byte limit by advertising a larger buffer size. If middleboxes drop EDNS0 packets or large UDP replies (>512 bytes), resolvers may experience timeouts or receive truncated responses. Standard behavior forces a fallback to TCP or raises a SERVFAIL if TCP is similarly blocked.
questions.hint: Think about traditional UDP payload size limits and what happens to modern security-signed zone records when packets grow too large.
questions.relatedConcept: DNS EDNS0 Extension Mechanisms and UDP Payload Size Limitations
questions.interviewTip: Tests deep understanding of DNS protocol extensions, middlebox behavior, and troubleshooting DNSSEC resolution failures.

questions.question: [Computer Networks • Test 1 • Q24] Why does an application layer protocol using HTTP/2 experience Head-of-Line (HoL) blocking at the transport layer, despite HTTP/2 multiplexing multiple streams over a single TCP connection?
options: TCP guarantees strict in-order byte delivery, so a single lost packet blocks all streams multiplexed within that TCP connection until retransmitted.
HTTP/2 enforces a strict round-robin frame serialization that pauses all active streams whenever a single request yields a 429 Too Many Requests status.
The TCP receive window is split statically among concurrent streams, causing a fast stream to stall if a slow stream exhausts its assigned sub-buffer.
TLS 1.3 record layer encryption prevents the client from acknowledging multiplexed frames individually.
questions.correctAnswer: TCP guarantees strict in-order byte delivery, so a single lost packet blocks all streams multiplexed within that TCP connection until retransmitted.
questions.explanation: While HTTP/2 solves application-layer HoL blocking by allowing multiple streams to interleave over one connection, it runs over TCP. Because TCP enforces reliable, in-order byte delivery, the loss of a single TCP segment stalls the entire TCP socket buffer—and consequently all multiplexed HTTP/2 streams—until the missing segment is successfully recovered.
questions.hint: Contrast application-layer stream multiplexing with transport-layer byte-stream guarantees.
questions.relatedConcept: Transport-Layer vs Application-Layer Head-of-Line Blocking in HTTP/2
questions.interviewTip: Frequently asked to evaluate why HTTP/3 (QUIC over UDP) was developed to replace HTTP/2 over TCP in lossy network conditions.

questions.question: [Computer Networks • Test 1 • Q25] What is the primary network-level consequence when a TCP socket has the TCP_NODELAY option enabled while the application frequently writes very small chunks of data?
options: The kernel buffers outgoing data until a full Maximum Segment Size (MSS) is accumulated, reducing packet count at the cost of latency.
Nagle's algorithm is disabled, causing the stack to immediately dispatch each small write as a separate TCP segment, potentially increasing packet overhead.
Delayed acknowledgments on the receiving side are permanently disabled to match the application's aggressive send rate.
The socket transitions into a constrained window state, forcing flow control to drop subsequent segments until an explicit window update is received.
questions.correctAnswer: Nagle's algorithm is disabled, causing the stack to immediately dispatch each small write as a separate TCP segment, potentially increasing packet overhead.
questions.explanation: Enabling TCP_NODELAY disables Nagle's algorithm, which normally buffers small outgoing packets to combine them into fewer, larger segments. Turning it off forces immediate transmission of small chunks, which reduces latency for interactive apps but increases total packet header overhead.
questions.hint: Think about what algorithm Nagle uses and what disabling it does to packet timing versus overhead.
questions.relatedConcept: TCP_NODELAY and Nagle's Algorithm interaction on packet size and transmission frequency
questions.interviewTip: Interviewers use this to test your understanding of the tradeoff between network throughput (packet efficiency) and application latency (responsiveness).

questions.question: [Computer Networks • Test 1 • Q26] In Linux networking, what is the exact operational effect of setting the SO_RCVBUF socket option to a lower value than the default?
options: It causes the kernel to immediately drop incoming packets that exceed the new threshold without attempting reassembly.
It disables the TCP window scaling option (RFC 1323) for that specific connection handle.
It restricts the maximum size of the TCP receive window advertised to the remote peer, thereby directly bounding the inflight data volume.
It truncates all incoming payload segments larger than the new buffer size before they reach application space.
questions.correctAnswer: It restricts the maximum size of the TCP receive window advertised to the remote peer, thereby directly bounding the inflight data volume.
questions.explanation: The socket receive buffer (SO_RCVBUF) directly dictates the upper bound of the TCP receive window advertised in ACKs. Lowering it restricts how much unacknowledged data the sender can transmit, which helps manage memory footprint but may limit maximum throughput on high-delay paths.
questions.hint: Consider how the receiver's buffer relates to flow control windows sent back to the sender.
questions.relatedConcept: Socket Receive Buffer Size (SO_RCVBUF) and TCP Receive Window scaling
questions.interviewTip: Crucial for systems programming and tuning high-concurrency network servers where memory consumption per socket must be tightly controlled.

questions.question: [Computer Networks • Test 1 • Q27] When utilizing HTTP/2 over TCP, multiple concurrent streams are multiplexed over a single TCP connection. What is the primary networking phenomenon that occurs when packet loss happens on that underlying TCP connection?
options: HTTP/2 automatically bypasses the lost packet by switching individual streams to separate ephemeral UDP sockets on the fly.
Only the specific HTTP/2 stream affected by the dropped packet experiences latency, while all other active streams continue completely unhindered.
The web browser instantly terminates the TCP connection and falls back to HTTP/1.1 pipelining without user notification.
Head-of-Line (HoL) blocking occurs at the TCP transport layer, stalling all multiplexed HTTP/2 streams regardless of whether their specific stream packets arrived safely.
questions.correctAnswer: Head-of-Line (HoL) blocking occurs at the TCP transport layer, stalling all multiplexed HTTP/2 streams regardless of whether their specific stream packets arrived safely.
questions.explanation: HTTP/2 solves application-layer head-of-line blocking by multiplexing streams over one TCP connection. However, it does not solve transport-layer head-of-line blocking: if TCP detects a lost packet, the entire TCP byte stream stalls until that packet is retransmitted and acknowledged, blocking all multiplexed HTTP/2 streams riding on top of it.
questions.hint: Think about what happens to a single underlying transport stream when a TCP sequence gap occurs.
questions.relatedConcept: HTTP/2 Transport Layer Head-of-Line Blocking
questions.interviewTip: Interviewers use this to test whether candidates understand the distinction between application-layer multiplexing and transport-layer reliability mechanisms.

questions.question: [Computer Networks • Test 1 • Q28] In distance-vector routing protocols such as RIP, what is the precise mechanism by which the 'Count-to-Infinity' problem is mitigated using 'Split Horizon with Poison Reverse'?
options: Routes learned from a neighbor via an interface are advertised back to that same neighbor with a metric of infinity (unreachable) rather than being suppressed entirely.
Routers completely shut down their interfaces whenever a neighbor's metric increases.
Routers wait for a fixed 5-minute hold-down timer before accepting any updates from adjacent nodes.
Routers encrypt routing table updates with dynamic keys to prevent rogue nodes from forging path metrics.
questions.correctAnswer: Routes learned from a neighbor via an interface are advertised back to that same neighbor with a metric of infinity (unreachable) rather than being suppressed entirely.
questions.explanation: Split Horizon with Poison Reverse actively advertises routes back to the neighbor from which they were learned, but explicitly sets their metric to infinity (e.g., 16 in RIP). This immediately overrides any stale routing loops by forcing neighbors to recognize the route is dead rather than waiting for timers to expire.
questions.hint: Consider how poisoning an advertised route prevents a downstream router from routing back through the sender.
questions.relatedConcept: Distance-Vector Routing and Split Horizon with Poison Reverse
questions.interviewTip: Often asked to evaluate deep understanding of routing protocol convergence loops and mitigation strategies.

questions.question: [Computer Networks • Test 1 • Q29] When troubleshooting a client-server connection, packet capture shows the client repeatedly retransmitting identical TCP segments while the server responds exclusively with cumulative ACKs acknowledging an old sequence number, but never advancing the window or sending data. What specific network condition or misconfiguration is indicated by this symptom pattern?
options: TCP Zero Window condition where the receiver's buffer is exhausted, coupled with periodic window probe exchanges
Asymmetric routing where the return path from the server traverses a different firewall that drops payload packets
A persistent TCP Silly Window Syndrome combined with delayed acknowledgement timeouts
An active TCP SYN-flood mitigation mechanism rate-limiting outbound segments at the kernel layer
questions.correctAnswer: Asymmetric routing where the return path from the server traverses a different firewall that drops payload packets
questions.explanation: When a client sends data segments that are continuously retransmitted while the server only acknowledges an older sequence number (often the beginning of the window) without advancing or closing with a zero window, it strongly implies that the traffic is taking an asymmetric path. The outbound path reaches the server, but the return path is intercepted, blocked, or dropped by a stateful firewall or routing policy that does not see the corresponding forward SYN state.
questions.hint: Consider what happens when forward and return paths diverge across middleboxes with stateful inspection.
questions.relatedConcept: Asymmetric Routing and Stateful Firewall Path Failures
questions.interviewTip: Interviewers use packet-walk scenarios to test if a candidate understands how stateful middleboxes interact with TCP packet flows.

questions.question: [Computer Networks • Test 1 • Q30] An administrator observes that HTTP/2 requests over a single TLS connection experience sudden, severe head-of-line blocking when a single packet is dropped on the underlying network path, whereas HTTP/1.1 pipelining or parallel connections did not suffer the exact same manifestation. What fundamental protocol design characteristic causes this behavior?
options: HTTP/2 enforces mandatory packet-level encryption interleaving that requires contiguous record decryption across all active request IDs.
The HTTP/2 HPACK compression context requires strict acknowledgment of header block fragments before any stream frame can be parsed.
HTTP/2 multiplexes multiple streams over a single TCP connection, forcing TCP's reliable in-order byte stream delivery to stall all streams until the lost packet is retransmitted.
HTTP/2 implements an application-layer flow control window that halts all stream multiplexing whenever a single frame checksum fails.
questions.correctAnswer: HTTP/2 multiplexes multiple streams over a single TCP connection, forcing TCP's reliable in-order byte stream delivery to stall all streams until the lost packet is retransmitted.
questions.explanation: HTTP/2 multiplexes multiple streams of requests and responses over a single TCP connection. Because TCP guarantees reliable, in-order delivery of the byte stream, a lost packet causes TCP to withhold all subsequent bytes from the application layer until the missing segment is recovered via retransmission. This stalls all multiplexed streams inside that connection, creating application-level head-of-line blocking at the transport layer.
questions.hint: Think about the relationship between application-layer multiplexing and transport-layer reliable byte streams.
questions.relatedConcept: HTTP/2 Transport-Layer Head-of-Line Blocking
questions.interviewTip: This tests whether candidates understand why HTTP/3 moved away from TCP to QUIC/UDP to solve transport-level head-of-line blocking.

questions.question: What is the primary operational difference between BGP (Border Gateway Protocol) operating as an eBGP session versus an iBGP session?
options: eBGP requires a fully meshed topology across all routers within an Autonomous System, whereas iBGP does not.
eBGP sets the NEXT_HOP attribute to the local router interface address by default, whereas iBGP typically preserves the NEXT_HOP learned from eBGP.
iBGP runs directly over TCP port 179 while eBGP runs over UDP port 179 for faster convergence.
eBGP relies on an underlying Interior Gateway Protocol to establish reachability, whereas iBGP does not require routing tables.
questions.correctAnswer: eBGP sets the NEXT_HOP attribute to the local router interface address by default, whereas iBGP typically preserves the NEXT_HOP learned from eBGP.
questions.explanation: When a router advertises a route to an eBGP peer, it modifies the NEXT_HOP attribute to its own IP address. Conversely, when advertising to an iBGP peer within the same Autonomous System, the NEXT_HOP attribute is normally preserved as received from the eBGP peer, unless explicitly modified using next-hop-self.
questions.hint: Consider how routing updates modify the NEXT_HOP path attribute when crossing Autonomous System boundaries versus internal paths.
questions.relatedConcept: BGP Path Attributes and eBGP/iBGP Hop Behavior
questions.interviewTip: Interviewers use this to test deep routing protocol mechanics beyond basic definition questions, focusing on path attribute modification rules.

title: Computer Networks - Test 2: Technical Assessment
description: Test 2 for Computer Networks. Every question is unique against the whole question database — no repeats, no renumbered or reworded variants of an existing question.

questions.question: What is the primary function of the 32-bit Random Number field in a DHCPv4 DISCOVER message?
options: It serves as an initial sequence number for TCP-like reliable delivery of DHCP options over UDP.
It is generated by the client to match incoming OFFER messages from multiple servers to the correct local instance.
It is used by the DHCP relay agent to encrypt the payload before forwarding it to the authoritative server.
It uniquely identifies the physical switch port to which the client interface is connected.
questions.correctAnswer: It is generated by the client to match incoming OFFER messages from multiple servers to the correct local instance.
questions.explanation: In DHCPv4, the 'xid' (transaction identifier) field is a 32-bit integer chosen randomly by the client. Since DHCP DISCOVER and REQUEST messages are broadcasted, multiple DHCP servers may respond with OFFER or ACK packets. The client uses this transaction ID to associate incoming responses with the correct pending request session.
questions.hint: Think about how a client distinguishes replies when multiple broadcast responses arrive.
questions.relatedConcept: DHCPv4 transaction identifier and packet matching
questions.interviewTip: Interviewers use this to test your understanding of layer-3 bootstrap protocols and how clients handle broadcast ambiguity.

questions.question: Why does the IEEE 802.3 Ethernet frame structure include a 4-byte Frame Check Sequence (FCS) at the end, while higher-layer protocols like TCP and IP also incorporate checksums?
options: Ethernet FCS is used strictly for cryptographic authentication, while TCP checksums are used for error recovery.
Higher-layer checksums are redundant and only exist for backward compatibility with non-Ethernet media, as the FCS guarantees complete end-to-end data integrity.

Ethernet FCS detects physical medium corruption (such as bit flips across the wire) allowing early frame drop, whereas transport/network checksums protect against software or end-to-end packet corruption.
The Ethernet FCS verifies only the MAC header, leaving payload error detection entirely to TCP and IP.
questions.correctAnswer: Ethernet FCS detects physical medium corruption (such as bit flips across the wire) allowing early frame drop, whereas transport/network checksums protect against software or end-to-end packet corruption.
questions.explanation: The data link layer FCS (CRC-32) operates hop-by-hop to catch physical transmission errors immediately on a specific link, preventing corrupted frames from wasting bandwidth further along the path. Transport (TCP) and network (IP) checksums operate end-to-end across multiple routers and potential memory/buffer corruption points inside intermediate nodes where the frame is re-framed.
questions.hint: Consider the difference between hop-by-hop physical link integrity and end-to-end path integrity across routers.
questions.relatedConcept: Layered error detection and end-to-end principle
questions.interviewTip: This tests the classic 'End-to-End Principle' in systems design and network architecture.

questions.question: What happens when a host running standard IP stack receives a UDP datagram destined for a local port that has no active socket bound to it?
options: The kernel buffers the datagram in a generic catch-all queue until a socket binds to that port.
The kernel broadcasts an ICMP Echo Request to discover if another host owns the port.
The operating system terminates the network interface driver to prevent buffer bloat.
The kernel drops the datagram silently and generates an ICMP Port Unreachable message.
questions.correctAnswer: The kernel drops the datagram silently and generates an ICMP Port Unreachable message.
questions.explanation: Unlike TCP, which maintains connection state and sends RST packets or drops silent segments depending on context, UDP is connectionless. When a UDP packet arrives at a closed port, the TCP/IP stack drops the payload and typically responds with an ICMP Destination Unreachable (specifically, Port Unreachable) message back to the sender, unless explicitly suppressed by firewall rules or local socket configurations.
questions.hint: Think about how connectionless protocols handle unrouted incoming delivery attempts.
questions.relatedConcept: UDP Port Unreachable ICMP Generation
questions.interviewTip: Interviewers use this to test your understanding of error reporting at the transport and network layers for connectionless protocols.

questions.question: In the context of Ethernet networks, what is the primary consequence of a 'late collision' occurring on a half-duplex shared medium?
options: The collision cannot be detected by the standard CSMA/CD collision detection mechanism, requiring higher-layer protocols for recovery.
The transmitting network interface automatically invokes its standard binary exponential backoff algorithm to resend the frame.
The receiving switch immediately drops all active frames on that VLAN and triggers a spanning tree reconfiguration.
The collision triggers a hardware interrupt that forces the physical layer transceiver to switch from half-duplex to full-duplex mode.
questions.correctAnswer: The collision cannot be detected by the standard CSMA/CD collision detection mechanism, requiring higher-layer protocols for recovery.
questions.explanation: A late collision is a collision that occurs after the first 512 bits (64 bytes) of a frame have been transmitted. Because standard CSMA/CD collision detection relies on the assumption that a collision will reach the sender within the slot time (the time it takes for a signal to propagate twice the maximum network distance), late collisions happen outside this window. Consequently, the transmitting NIC's hardware cannot detect them, and reliability must be handled by transport-layer or application-layer acknowledgments.
questions.hint: Consider the timing constraints of CSMA/CD and the minimum frame size.
questions.relatedConcept: Ethernet Late Collisions and CSMA/CD Timing
questions.interviewTip: This tests deep knowledge of physical/data-link layer mechanics and legacy half-duplex network troubleshooting.

questions.question: What is the primary architectural advantage of utilizing Jumbo Frames (MTU around 9000 bytes) in high-performance data center networks?
options: It eliminates packet loss entirely by preventing buffer overflows at intermediate layer-3 switches.
It significantly reduces CPU interrupt overhead by decreasing the total number of packets that must be processed for a given payload volume.
It completely removes the need for TCP segmentation offloading (TSO) on Network Interface Cards.
It increases the physical speed of light propagation through copper and fiber-optic cabling.
questions.correctAnswer: It significantly reduces CPU interrupt overhead by decreasing the total number of packets that must be processed for a given payload volume.
questions.explanation: Jumbo frames increase the Ethernet payload size from ~1500 bytes to ~9000 bytes. This means fewer packets are generated for large data transfers, directly lowering per-packet OS processing and interrupt handling overhead on host CPUs. They do not eliminate packet loss, replace TSO, or change propagation speed.
questions.hint: Think about the host CPU cost incurred per transmitted packet regardless of its size.
questions.relatedConcept: Network performance trade-offs involving Maximum Transmission Unit (MTU) sizing
questions.interviewTip: Interviewers use this to test your understanding of systems-level networking bottlenecks, specifically how packet rate affects CPU load compared to throughput.

questions.question: Why does enabling Path MTU Discovery (PMTUD) incorrectly in an environment with asymmetric routing or overly aggressive firewalls often lead to 'black hole' connection hangs?
options: The receiving host intentionally drops TCP SYN-ACK packets if their TTL value exceeds the configured MTU threshold.
Asymmetric paths cause sequence numbers to randomize unexpectedly, corrupting the negotiated MTU payload value.
Routers drop oversized packets and fail to return the necessary ICMP Destination Unreachable (Fragmentation Needed) messages back to the sender.
Firewalls automatically ban IP addresses that attempt to transmit packets larger than 576 bytes.
questions.correctAnswer: Routers drop oversized packets and fail to return the necessary ICMP Destination Unreachable (Fragmentation Needed) messages back to the sender.
questions.explanation: Path MTU Discovery relies on routers returning ICMP Type 3 Code 4 (Fragmentation Needed) messages when a packet exceeds an outgoing link's MTU and the Don't Fragment (DF) bit is set. If middleboxes or security firewalls drop these ICMP messages, the sender never learns the reduced MTU and continues transmitting packets that get dropped silently, causing a connection hang.
questions.hint: Consider which ICMP control messages are critical for a sender to adjust its transmission packet size dynamically.
questions.relatedConcept: Path MTU Discovery failure modes and ICMP filtering side-effects
questions.interviewTip: A classic troubleshooting question used to assess whether a candidate understands the interplay between layer-3 routing, control plane ICMP messaging, and layer-4 transport reliability.

questions.question: When configuring a Linux bridge or a virtual switch (like Open vSwitch) to interconnect multiple virtual machines, what fundamental hazard occurs if a routing loop forms at Layer 2 without spanning tree protocols (STP/RSTP) enabled?
options: Automatic IP address reassignment conflicts due to continuous DHCP DISCOVER broadcasts being modified in-flight.
Immediate kernel panic on the virtualization host caused by unhandled interrupt request saturation.
Packet sequence numbering desynchronization across all transport layer TCP connections traversing the bridge.
Broadcast storms due to continuous frame replication and looping, leading to exponential traffic amplification and network collapse.
questions.correctAnswer: Broadcast storms due to continuous frame replication and looping, leading to exponential traffic amplification and network collapse.
questions.explanation: At Layer 2, Ethernet frames do not possess a Time-To-Live (TTL) or hop-count decrement field unlike IP packets at Layer 3. Therefore, if a physical or virtual bridging loop exists without STP or a loop-prevention mechanism, broadcast, unknown unicast, and multicast (BUM) traffic will circulate indefinitely, consuming all available bandwidth and CPU cycles, known as a broadcast storm.
questions.hint: Think about what prevents Ethernet frames from circulating forever like IP packets do.
questions.relatedConcept: Layer 2 bridging loops and broadcast storm amplification
questions.interviewTip: Interviewers use this to test your understanding of the fundamental difference in loop mitigation between Layer 2 (no TTL) and Layer 3.

questions.question: What is the primary architectural justification for utilizing UDP-based transport protocols like QUIC over traditional TCP in modern high-performance web transport architectures?
options: QUIC implements application-layer framing with independent stream multiplexing, completely eliminating Head-of-Line (HoL) blocking across streams.
QUIC forces all packets through kernel-space TCP state machines to bypass user-space context switching bottlenecks.
QUIC relies on connection-oriented three-way handshakes that encrypt packet headers at the data link layer.
QUIC automatically increases packet transmission rates beyond the bottleneck bandwidth by ignoring congestion notification signals.
questions.correctAnswer: QUIC implements application-layer framing with independent stream multiplexing, completely eliminating Head-of-Line (HoL) blocking across streams.
questions.explanation: In traditional HTTP/2 over TCP, if a single TCP segment is lost, the entire TCP byte-stream stalls, blocking all concurrent streams multiplexed over that connection (Transport-layer Head-of-Line blocking). QUIC runs over UDP and implements independent stream multiplexing, meaning packet loss on one stream does not stall data delivery on other streams.
questions.hint: Consider how TCP handles lost segments versus how QUIC isolates streams.
questions.relatedConcept: QUIC transport protocol stream multiplexing and HoL blocking mitigation
questions.interviewTip: Essential networking architecture question; frequently used to see if a candidate understands modern transport protocols beyond standard TCP.

questions.question: What is the primary operational consequence when an operating system's network stack runs completely out of mbufs or socket buffer memory while receiving incoming TCP segments?
options: The kernel automatically migrates excess socket buffers to user-space virtual memory via page file swapping.
The kernel drops the incoming segments silently, which eventually causes the remote sender's congestion window to stall and trigger retransmissions.
The network interface card (NIC) immediately raises a hardware fault interrupt that halts the operating system kernel.
The TCP receiver immediately sends a RST (reset) packet to abruptly terminate the connection.
questions.correctAnswer: The kernel drops the incoming segments silently, which eventually causes the remote sender's congestion window to stall and trigger retransmissions.
questions.explanation: When socket buffers or kernel mbufs are exhausted, the OS network stack cannot allocate memory to queue incoming segments, forcing it to drop them. The sender's lack of acknowledgments leads to timeouts and retransmissions. It does not crash the OS or send a RST immediately.
questions.hint: Consider what the kernel does with data packets when it has nowhere to store them.
questions.relatedConcept: Network buffer exhaustion and memory management in OS transport layers
questions.interviewTip: Interviewers use this to test your understanding of how low-level OS resource constraints interact with transport-layer reliability mechanisms.

questions.question: How does Linux handle socket buffer memory allocation dynamically when the 'tcp_rmem' or 'tcp_wmem' tuning parameters are left at their default auto-tuning state?
options: The kernel pre-allocates the maximum allowable buffer size for every newly created socket to completely prevent memory reallocation overhead.
The kernel disables all TCP window scaling to restrict memory consumption to a strict fixed ceiling of 64 kilobytes per flow.
The kernel dynamically adjusts the receive and send buffer sizes for each active TCP socket based on measured bandwidth-delay product and memory pressure.
The kernel relies entirely on user-space applications to explicitly request memory allocations via setsockopt() before every packet arrival.
questions.correctAnswer: The kernel dynamically adjusts the receive and send buffer sizes for each active TCP socket based on measured bandwidth-delay product and memory pressure.
questions.explanation: Linux TCP memory auto-tuning dynamically scales socket buffer sizes per connection based on the estimated bandwidth-delay product (BDP) and system-wide memory availability, balancing throughput and resource consumption.
questions.hint: Think about how modern OSes balance memory usage across thousands of concurrent TCP connections without starving the system.
questions.relatedConcept: TCP socket buffer auto-tuning and kernel memory management
questions.interviewTip: Useful for assessing whether a candidate understands kernel tuning parameters and memory footprint implications in high-concurrency servers.

questions.question: What is the primary function of the IGMP (Internet Group Management Protocol) Snooping mechanism implemented in modern network switches?
options: It translates multicast IP addresses into dynamic MAC addresses for hardware-level packet filtering.
It blocks broadcast storm traffic by automatically rate-limiting ARP requests on access ports.
It monitors spanning tree topology changes to prevent multicast loops in redundant ring architectures.
It inspects IGMP join and leave messages to dynamically forward multicast traffic only to ports that have interested receivers.
questions.correctAnswer: It inspects IGMP join and leave messages to dynamically forward multicast traffic only to ports that have interested receivers.
questions.explanation: IGMP Snooping allows a layer-2 switch to listen to IGMP conversation between hosts and routers, mapping multicast groups to specific switch ports so that multicast traffic isn't flooded to every port like broadcast traffic.
questions.hint: Think about how switches handle multicast traffic optimization at Layer 2.
questions.relatedConcept: IGMP Snooping optimization
questions.interviewTip: Interviewers often ask this to verify your understanding of how Layer 2 devices handle Layer 3 multicast optimization without full routing capabilities.

questions.question: Why does the HTTP/2 protocol multiplex multiple request-streams over a single TCP connection, yet applications still sometimes experience 'head-of-line blocking'?
options: Because packet loss at the underlying TCP transport layer causes the entire TCP socket buffer to stall, blocking all HTTP/2 streams regardless of application-layer multiplexing.
Because HTTP/2 enforces strict sequential execution of GET requests at the client browser cache level.
Because TLS record encryption requires streams to be decrypted in exact numerical order before being processed by the application.
Because HTTP/2 multiplexing only supports a maximum of two concurrent streams per TCP connection by default.
questions.correctAnswer: Because packet loss at the underlying TCP transport layer causes the entire TCP socket buffer to stall, blocking all HTTP/2 streams regardless of application-layer multiplexing.
questions.explanation: Although HTTP/2 eliminates application-level head-of-line blocking by multiplexing streams over one TCP connection, TCP itself enforces reliable in-order delivery. If a single TCP packet is dropped, subsequent packets cannot be delivered to the application layer until the lost packet is retransmitted, stalling all HTTP/2 streams.
questions.hint: Consider the difference between application-layer multiplexing and transport-layer reliability guarantees.
questions.relatedConcept: HTTP/2 Transport Head-of-Line Blocking
questions.interviewTip: This is a classic systems-architecture question that tests whether you understand layer interactions, specifically why HTTP/3 moved to UDP (QUIC).

questions.question: When troubleshooting a network path using traceroute, an engineer notices that consecutive routers along the path return ICMP Time Exceeded messages, but the final destination IP address responds with ICMP Port Unreachable. What does this specific combination of ICMP messages indicate about the packet flow?
options: A firewall at the penultimate hop is blocking the final transport-layer segment while allowing intermediary router TTL decrements.
The packets successfully traversed the entire path and reached the destination host, where they hit a closed UDP port.
The destination host is down, causing intermediate routers to simulate replies until timeout.
The network is experiencing asymmetric routing where the return path traverses a different set of autonomous systems.
questions.correctAnswer: The packets successfully traversed the entire path and reached the destination host, where they hit a closed UDP port.
questions.explanation: Traceroute typically sends UDP packets with incrementing TTLs to high-numbered ports. Each intermediate router decrements the TTL to 0 and returns an ICMP Time Exceeded message. Once the packet reaches the target host, since the port is unused/closed, the host itself generates an ICMP Port Unreachable message, confirming full end-to-end delivery.
questions.hint: Think about how standard traceroute implementations probe ports and how the final destination distinguishes itself from intermediate routers.
questions.relatedConcept: ICMP error message semantics in path diagnostic tools
questions.interviewTip: Interviewers use traceroute diagnostic questions to test whether candidates understand the layer-4 payload encapsulated within probe packets versus layer-3 control messages.

questions.question: An administrator monitoring a high-traffic Linux server observes thousands of TCP connections stuck in the CLOSE_WAIT state. What does this symptom definitively imply about the state of the application layer on the local host?
options: The local application crashed before acknowledging the final ACK of the four-way handshake.
The remote peer is flooding the local host with SYN packets faster than the TCP stack can allocate buffers.
The local application has failed to call close() on the socket after receiving a FIN from the remote peer.
Network congestion is delaying the transmission of the local host's ACK packet back to the remote peer.
questions.correctAnswer: The local application has failed to call close() on the socket after receiving a FIN from the remote peer.
questions.explanation: CLOSE_WAIT means the local TCP stack has received a connection termination request (FIN) from the remote side and acknowledged it, transitioning to CLOSE_WAIT while waiting for the local application process to finish reading remaining data and explicitly invoke close(). Sticking in this state points directly to an application-side leak where sockets are left unclosed.
questions.hint: Recall which entity initiates the connection termination and what responsibility the passive closer has before sending its own FIN.
questions.relatedConcept: TCP connection state machine troubleshooting (CLOSE_WAIT root cause)
questions.interviewTip: This is a classic systems-networking crossover question that separates candidates who only know TCP theory from those who have debugged production socket leaks.

questions.question: When utilizing DNS resolution via standard system libraries (e.g., `getaddrinfo`), what occurs when an application queries a domain name whose authoritative nameservers are entirely unreachable, but valid records exist in the local stub resolver's cache?
options: The stub resolver queries the root nameservers anyway, triggering a network timeout before falling back to the cache.
The function fails immediately with an EAI_FAIL error because cache validation requires at least one active upstream query.
The function blocks for the duration of the default network timeout before inspecting the cache.
The stub resolver returns the cached records immediately without attempting network communication, ignoring the downtime of authoritative servers.
questions.correctAnswer: The stub resolver returns the cached records immediately without attempting network communication, ignoring the downtime of authoritative servers.
questions.explanation: Standard stub resolvers check their local cache first. If a valid, non-expired record is found, it is returned immediately to the application without querying upstream authoritative servers, regardless of the current network reachability of those servers.
questions.hint: Think about what caching achieves when upstream servers go offline.
questions.relatedConcept: DNS stub resolver caching behavior under upstream network partitioning
questions.interviewTip: Interviewers use this to test your understanding of how application-layer networking APIs interact with local caching layers versus live network calls.

questions.question: In HTTP/2 connection management over TCP, how does an endpoint handle the receipt of a GOAWAY frame from its peer while it has multiple active, in-flight stream requests?
options: It stops creating new streams on that connection, but continues processing and receiving responses for streams already initiated with IDs lower than the last-stream-ID specified in the GOAWAY frame.
It must immediately terminate all current streams and close the underlying TCP connection.
It automatically retries all active streams on a newly established HTTP/1.1 fallback connection.
It pauses the TCP socket using socket-level flow control until the peer sends a RESUME frame.
questions.correctAnswer: It stops creating new streams on that connection, but continues processing and receiving responses for streams already initiated with IDs lower than the last-stream-ID specified in the GOAWAY frame.
questions.explanation: The HTTP/2 GOAWAY frame allows an endpoint to gracefully shut down a connection. The sender of GOAWAY specifies the last stream ID it successfully processed. The receiver must stop initiating new streams on that connection but can finish processing active streams that fall within the valid range.
questions.hint: Consider graceful connection teardown semantics in multiplexed protocols.
questions.relatedConcept: HTTP/2 GOAWAY frame lifecycle and stream draining semantics
questions.interviewTip: Crucial for backend engineers designing high-throughput microservices communicating over persistent HTTP/2 or gRPC connections.

questions.question: What is the primary operational consequence of enabling Path MTU Discovery (PMTUD) when intermediate routers drop a packet exceeding their link MTU but fail to set the IPv4 Don't Fragment (DF) bit or the IPv6 packet is simply too large?
options: Intermediate routers automatically fragment the packet in transit despite the constraints and forward it downstream.
Black hole connections occur where packets silently drop without generating ICMP Fragmentation Needed messages, stalling communication.
The transport layer automatically switches to a fixed 576-byte fallback maximum segment size for all subsequent sockets.
The destination host actively renegotiates the physical layer baud rate to accommodate oversized frames.
questions.correctAnswer: Black hole connections occur where packets silently drop without generating ICMP Fragmentation Needed messages, stalling communication.
questions.explanation: Path MTU Discovery relies on ICMP 'Destination Unreachable: Fragmentation Needed' (IPv4) or 'Packet Too Big' (IPv6) messages from routers to inform the sender to lower its MSS. If firewalls or routers block these ICMP messages, the sender continues transmitting oversized packets, resulting in a 'PMTUD black hole' where connections hang indefinitely.
questions.hint: Consider what happens when critical error notification messages are blocked by security firewalls along the path.
questions.relatedConcept: Path MTU Discovery black hole problem and ICMP filtering
questions.interviewTip: Interviewers use this to test deep knowledge of internet layer diagnostics, MTU issues, and how ICMP filtering can paradoxically break higher-layer TCP connections.

questions.question: In IEEE 802.11 wireless networks, how does the RTS/CTS (Request to Send / Clear to Send) mechanism mitigate the hidden node problem?
options: By dynamically encrypting packet headers so that hidden nodes cannot intercept or interfere with frame payload data.
By cycling through orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing subcarriers until a clear channel is found without collisions.
By having transmitting stations reserve the medium and alert all listening nodes within range of both the sender and receiver to defer transmission.
By forcing all client stations to communicate exclusively through polling requests managed directly by the access point.
questions.correctAnswer: By having transmitting stations reserve the medium and alert all listening nodes within range of both the sender and receiver to defer transmission.
questions.explanation: The hidden node problem occurs when two nodes cannot hear each other but can both reach a common access point. By sending an RTS frame (which the AP acknowledges with a CTS frame containing a network allocation vector duration), neighboring nodes within range of either the sender or receiver learn of the upcoming transmission and defer access.
questions.hint: Think about how stations out of direct range of each other are informed about medium reservation through shared intermediaries.
questions.relatedConcept: IEEE 802.11 MAC layer, hidden node problem, and RTS/CTS handshake
questions.interviewTip: This tests understanding of wireless medium access control nuances beyond basic CSMA/CD principles used in wired Ethernet.

questions.question: When configuring a network monitoring tool using SNMPv3, which security level combines message authentication with encryption to ensure both data integrity and confidentiality for telemetry data?
options: authNoPriv
noAuthNoPriv
encNoAuth
authPriv
questions.correctAnswer: authPriv
questions.explanation: In SNMPv3, the 'authPriv' security level provides both authentication (verifying message integrity and sender identity) and privacy/encryption (protecting data confidentiality). 'authNoPriv' provides authentication without encryption, 'noAuthNoPriv' provides neither, and 'encNoAuth' is not a valid standard SNMPv3 security level combination.
questions.hint: Look for the mode that explicitly includes both authentication and privacy (encryption).
questions.relatedConcept: SNMPv3 security levels and diagnostic telemetry configuration
questions.interviewTip: Interviewers ask about SNMPv3 to verify your understanding of securing network management and monitoring planes against eavesdropping and tampering.

questions.question: When capturing network packets using libpcap-based tools like tcpdump, what is the primary consequence of configuring an oversized snapshot length (snaplen) larger than the Maximum Transmission Unit (MTU) of the underlying interface?
options: It consumes more memory per packet buffer in ring buffers without capturing any additional payload beyond the actual frame size.
It causes the network interface card (NIC) to drop incoming frames due to buffer overflow validation errors.
It automatically forces the interface into promiscuous mode regardless of command-line flags.
It triggers software-level IP fragmentation on all outgoing diagnostic probe packets.
questions.correctAnswer: It consumes more memory per packet buffer in ring buffers without capturing any additional payload beyond the actual frame size.
questions.explanation: A snapshot length (snaplen) limits how many bytes of each frame are stored in the capture buffer. Setting it larger than the physical MTU means memory is needlessly allocated for potential payload lengths that will never physically arrive on that medium, wasting ring buffer space. It does not drop packets, force promiscuous mode, or trigger IP fragmentation.
questions.hint: Consider what happens to buffer allocation when you ask a capture tool to store more bytes than can possibly fit into an Ethernet frame.
questions.relatedConcept: Packet capture internals, snaplen configuration, and diagnostic buffer management
questions.interviewTip: Interviewers use this to test whether candidates understand the low-level constraints and performance tuning of packet sniffing and troubleshooting utilities.

questions.question: What is the primary security vulnerability or operational issue when configuring an SNMPv2c agent with a weak, publicly known community string while permitting unrestricted read-write access from any external IP address?
options: Encrypted payload interception via man-in-the-middle attacks due to absent Diffie-Hellman key exchanges
Unauthorized remote modification of device configuration parameters and information leakage via MIB walking
Automatic generation of UDP broadcast loops that lead to spanning tree topology collapses
Immediate kernel panic on network switches due to unvalidated ASN.1 buffer overflow exploits in traps
questions.correctAnswer: Unauthorized remote modification of device configuration parameters and information leakage via MIB walking
questions.explanation: SNMPv2c relies entirely on cleartext community strings for authentication. If a write community string is weak and exposure is global, any remote attacker can perform arbitrary configuration modifications (via SetRequests) and extract sensitive network topology details via MIB walking.
questions.hint: Think about how SNMPv2c authenticates managers to agents and what capabilities community strings grant.
questions.relatedConcept: SNMPv2c authentication vulnerabilities and community string exposure
questions.interviewTip: Interviewers use this to test knowledge of legacy protocol vulnerabilities that lack modern cryptographic integrity and confidentiality.

questions.question: In the context of IPv6 ICMPv6 Neighbor Discovery, what security risk is introduced when Router Advertisement (RA) Guard is disabled on edge switch ports facing untrusted user access segments?
options: Attackers can flood the local subnet with Neighbor Solicitation messages carrying spoofed MAC addresses, exhausting switch CAM tables
Unauthenticated nodes can force the core router to drop into an infinite loop by fragmenting ICMPv6 error messages beyond the MTU
Rogue hosts can inject arbitrary unsolicited Router Advertisements to perform Man-in-the-Middle attacks via fraudulent gateway or prefix assignments
Neighbor Cache entries become permanently pinned, preventing legitimate IP address reassignments during DHCPv6 lease renewal
questions.correctAnswer: Rogue hosts can inject arbitrary unsolicited Router Advertisements to perform Man-in-the-Middle attacks via fraudulent gateway or prefix assignments
questions.explanation: Without RA Guard, any host on the local segment can transmit rogue Router Advertisement messages, allowing malicious nodes to spoof the default gateway, manipulate prefix configurations, or execute SLAAC-based redirection attacks leading to traffic interception.
questions.hint: Consider what happens when an unauthorized device pretends to be the router on a broadcast domain.
questions.relatedConcept: ICMPv6 Router Advertisement spoofing and RA Guard mitigation
questions.interviewTip: Evaluates candidate awareness of Layer 2 security extensions required for IPv6 deployments where ARP spoofing equivalents exist.

questions.question: What is the primary architectural benefit of utilizing VXLAN (Virtual Extensible LAN) over traditional VLANs in large-scale multi-tenant data center cloud environments?
options: It eliminates the need for any underlying layer 3 routing infrastructure by bridging Ethernet frames natively across wide area networks.
It reduces the MTU overhead on physical switch interfaces by dynamically compressing inner TCP/IP headers.
It enforces strict MAC address learning synchronization across disparate geographic regions without requiring multicast flooding.
It overcomes the 12-bit VLAN ID limit of 4,096 distinct networks by using a 24-bit segment identifier (VNI) supporting up to 16 million logical networks.
questions.correctAnswer: It overcomes the 12-bit VLAN ID limit of 4,096 distinct networks by using a 24-bit segment identifier (VNI) supporting up to 16 million logical networks.
questions.explanation: Traditional VLANs use a 12-bit tag field in the IEEE 802.1Q header, limiting the maximum number of isolated networks to 4,096. VXLAN introduces a 24-bit VNI (VXLAN Network Identifier), expanding this limit to 16 million, which is critical for massive cloud-scale tenant isolation.
questions.hint: Consider the bit-width limitations of legacy layer 2 frame tagging schemes.
questions.relatedConcept: VXLAN 24-bit VNI scaling vs traditional 12-bit VLAN limitations
questions.interviewTip: Interviewers use this to test your understanding of data center virtualization challenges and overlay network protocols.

questions.question: In distance-vector routing protocols like RIP, what specific failure scenario does the 'Split Horizon with Poison Reverse' mechanism directly mitigate?
options: The count-to-infinity loop caused by a router advertising a route back to the next-hop neighbor from which it learned the route.
The formation of asymmetric routing paths when link-state metrics fluctuate due to asymmetrical interface bandwidth.
The premature expiration of routing table entries during temporary control-plane CPU starvation spikes.
The silent black-holing of packets when an intermediate autonomous system border router drops BGP attributes.
questions.correctAnswer: The count-to-infinity loop caused by a router advertising a route back to the next-hop neighbor from which it learned the route.
questions.explanation: Split Horizon prevents a router from advertising a route back out the interface it learned it from. Poison Reverse takes it further by advertising that route back to the neighbor with an infinite metric (cost of 16 in RIP) to immediately poison and invalidate any potential loop.
questions.hint: Think about routing loops caused by stale neighbor information in distance-vector algorithms.
questions.relatedConcept: Split Horizon with Poison Reverse in distance-vector routing
questions.interviewTip: Expect this when discussing fundamental routing protocol robustness and loop-prevention mechanics.

questions.question: What is the primary operational consequence when a router receives an IPv4 packet with the Don't Fragment (DF) bit set, and the packet's size exceeds the outgoing link's Maximum Transmission Unit (MTU)?
options: The router automatically fragments the packet into smaller segments and clears the DF bit for downstream transmission.
The router drops the packet and sends an ICMP Destination Unreachable message (Type 3, Code 4) back to the source.
The router buffers the packet in memory until a path with a larger MTU becomes available.
The router encapsulates the packet in a GRE tunnel to bypass the MTU limitation.
questions.correctAnswer: The router drops the packet and sends an ICMP Destination Unreachable message (Type 3, Code 4) back to the source.
questions.explanation: When the DF (Don't Fragment) bit is set in the IPv4 header, routers are strictly prohibited from fragmenting the packet. If the packet exceeds the outgoing interface's MTU, the router must drop it and generate an ICMP Destination Unreachable (Fragmentation Needed and DF Set) message back to the sender to facilitate Path MTU Discovery.
questions.hint: Think about what the 'Don't Fragment' bit strictly commands the router to do when an interface constraint is encountered.
questions.relatedConcept: IPv4 Path MTU Discovery and DF bit handling
questions.interviewTip: Interviewers use this to test your understanding of IP layer flags, error reporting mechanisms (ICMP), and how modern MTU discovery operates.

questions.question: In the context of standard Ethernet bridging and local area networks, what is the precise primary purpose of the Spanning Tree Protocol (STP) root bridge?
options: It inspects and translates all inter-VLAN routing tables so switches can communicate without a layer-3 router.
It dynamically assigns IP addresses to all connected switch management interfaces via a built-in DHCP relay.
It acts as the reference point for calculating path costs and determining port roles across the entire switched topology.
It acts as the centralized gateway that encapsulates and forwards all broadcast storms to prevent network saturation.
questions.correctAnswer: It acts as the reference point for calculating path costs and determining port roles across the entire switched topology.
questions.explanation: The root bridge in STP serves as the logical center of the spanning tree topology. All path cost calculations, root port selections, and designated port determinations are calculated relative to this elected reference bridge to prevent permanent physical loops.
questions.hint: Consider how switches coordinate topology calculations without a centralized router.
questions.relatedConcept: Spanning Tree Protocol Root Bridge Election and Topology Calculation
questions.interviewTip: Strong candidates should be able to explain layer-2 control plane protocols beyond just 'preventing loops' by detailing how topology calculations depend on a reference node.

questions.question: What happens at the transport and network layers when a host application attempts to send a UDP datagram whose size exceeds the path Maximum Transmission Unit (MTU), assuming the Don't Fragment (DF) bit is set in the IPv4 header?
options: The transport layer automatically segments the datagram into smaller fragments, reassembling them transparently at the destination receiver.
The network interface card (NIC) automatically fragments the IP packet into frames matching the MTU size.
The router upstream drops the packet and may send an ICMP Destination Unreachable (Fragmentation Needed) message back to the source.
The kernel drops the packet immediately and returns an EMSGSIZE (Message too long) error to the sending application without transmitting anything over the wire.
questions.correctAnswer: The kernel drops the packet immediately and returns an EMSGSIZE (Message too long) error to the sending application without transmitting anything over the wire.
questions.explanation: Unlike TCP, which handles segmentation via MSS negotiation and stream chunking, UDP is a datagram protocol. If a user application hands down a datagram larger than the interface MTU with the DF bit set, the local IP stack refuses to fragment it locally and fails the send operation directly by returning an EMSGSIZE error to the user space.
questions.hint: Consider whether UDP has a built-in session-layer segmentation mechanism like TCP.
questions.relatedConcept: UDP datagram size limits and local stack handling of DF bit
questions.interviewTip: Interviewers use this to test whether candidates understand the fundamental API boundary differences between connection-oriented stream sockets (TCP) and connectionless datagram sockets (UDP).

questions.question: In a high-throughput Linux network stack, what is the primary consequence of setting the socket option `SO_RCVBUF` to a value significantly smaller than the Bandwidth-Delay Product (BDP) on a high-latency link?
options: The operating system shrinks the TCP Receive Window (Rwin) advertised in ACK packets, limiting the sender's unacknowledged data in flight and capping maximum throughput.
The TCP sender's congestion window is artificially inflated past network capacity, causing immediate bufferbloat.
The kernel drops outgoing segments due to local socket queue exhaustion.
The network interface driver switches from interrupt-driven mode to NAPI polling mode prematurely.
questions.correctAnswer: The operating system shrinks the TCP Receive Window (Rwin) advertised in ACK packets, limiting the sender's unacknowledged data in flight and capping maximum throughput.
questions.explanation: The TCP Receive Window (advertised in the window field of the TCP header) is bounded by the available space in the socket's receive buffer (`SO_RCVBUF`). If this buffer is set smaller than the BDP, the receiver cannot advertise enough window to keep the pipe full, severely limiting throughput on high-latency connections regardless of available bandwidth.
questions.hint: Think about how the receiver advertises flow control limits back to the sender.
questions.relatedConcept: TCP Receive Buffer sizing and Bandwidth-Delay Product limitation
questions.interviewTip: This question assesses deep systems-level understanding of TCP flow control, window scaling, and performance tuning on long-fat networks (LFNs).

questions.question: What is the primary architectural advantage of utilizing Path MTU Discovery (PMTUD) in IP networks, and what vulnerability does it introduce if improperly handled?
options: It speeds up TCP slow-start convergence by dynamically resizing the MSS; missing ICMP messages result in excessive retransmissions.
It prevents packet fragmentation by determining the smallest MTU along the path; improper ICMP filtering can cause silent connection black holes.
It allows routers to fragment packets at line rate using hardware offloads; missing ICMP triggers infinite routing loops.
It completely eliminates the need for TCP Maximum Segment Size negotiation; blocked ICMP messages lead to connection resets.
questions.correctAnswer: It prevents packet fragmentation by determining the smallest MTU along the path; improper ICMP filtering can cause silent connection black holes.
questions.explanation: PMTUD dynamically discovers the minimum MTU along a network path using ICMP 'Fragmentation Needed' messages, preventing router fragmentation overhead. However, if firewalls overly restrict ICMP Type 3 messages, nodes never receive the update, leading to frustrating connection stalls known as Path MTU black holes.
questions.hint: Think about what ICMP messages are required when a router encounters a packet larger than the outgoing link MTU.
questions.relatedConcept: Path MTU Discovery and ICMP black hole dynamics
questions.interviewTip: Interviewers use this to test deep knowledge of IP layer behavior and how transport layer protocols interact with firewall configurations.

questions.question: In software-defined networking (SDN) architectures using OpenFlow, what is the trade-off between proactive and reactive flow entry installation?
options: Reactive installation maximizes switch TCAM utilization, whereas proactive installation causes high CPU utilization on the controller for every packet.
Proactive installation eliminates all packet drops during congestion, whereas reactive installation relies completely on underlying spanning-tree topology.
Reactive installation introduces initial packet setup latency and control-plane overhead, whereas proactive installation consumes switch flow-table memory for unused paths.
Proactive installation speeds up dynamic traffic engineering, whereas reactive installation requires all switches to run BGP routing daemons.
questions.correctAnswer: Reactive installation introduces initial packet setup latency and control-plane overhead, whereas proactive installation consumes switch flow-table memory for unused paths.
questions.explanation: Reactive flow setup requires the first packet of a new flow to be sent up to the controller, adding latency and control-channel load. Proactive setup populates rules ahead of time, avoiding control-plane bottlenecks but wasting precious TCAM memory on switches for routes that may never be used.
questions.hint: Consider the burden on switch memory versus controller response time when dealing with unpredictable traffic flows.
questions.relatedConcept: OpenFlow proactive vs. reactive flow installation trade-offs
questions.interviewTip: Useful for assessing a candidate's understanding of control-plane versus data-plane separation and resource scaling in SDN.

questions.question: In BGP (Border Gateway Protocol), what is the primary purpose of the 'MED' (Multi-Exit Discriminator) optional non-transitive attribute?
options: It forces all routers within an Autonomous System to prioritize routes originating from a specific internal IGP metric.
It acts as a suggestion to external neighbor ASes on the preferred entry point into the local AS when multiple interconnect links exist.
It prevents routing loops across different confederations by incrementing a hop-count value at each AS boundary.
It assigns an administrative preference value that overrides all other local path selection rules regardless of AS path length.
questions.correctAnswer: It acts as a suggestion to external neighbor ASes on the preferred entry point into the local AS when multiple interconnect links exist.
questions.explanation: The Multi-Exit Discriminator (MED) is an optional non-transitive attribute used to communicate to an adjacent Autonomous System (AS) which of multiple entry points is preferred for entering the local AS. Because it is non-transitive, the receiving AS does not pass it along to further ASes.
questions.hint: Think about how an AS with multiple redundant peering connections tells a neighboring AS which link to prefer.
questions.relatedConcept: BGP Path Attributes (MED)
questions.interviewTip: Interviewer asks this to test deep knowledge of inter-domain routing protocols and path selection criteria beyond basic eBGP/iBGP configuration.

title: Computer Vision - Test 1: Core Fundamentals & Patterns
description: Comprehensive technical evaluation for Computer Vision covering runtime mechanics, design principles, and problem solving.

questions.question: [Computer Vision • Test 1 • Q1] In Python OpenCV, why is explicit channel reordering necessary after reading a color image with `cv2.imread` before processing it with libraries like PIL or scikit-image?
options: OpenCV stores pixel data row-major while PIL stores it column-major, requiring a reshaping transpose.
OpenCV encodes color channels in BGR order rather than the standard RGB order used by most PIL and scikit-image functions.
OpenCV normalizes float values to [0,1] while PIL expects 8-bit integers, causing underflow if not cast.
OpenCV excludes the alpha channel by default, forcing manual concatenation if transparency is present.
questions.correctAnswer: OpenCV encodes color channels in BGR order rather than the standard RGB order used by most PIL and scikit-image functions.
questions.explanation: The fundamental difference is the channel ordering: OpenCV uses BGR, while PIL and scikit-image use RGB. Without `cv2.cvtColor(img, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB)`, the red and blue channels are swapped in subsequent processing.
questions.hint: Consider the hex color of a pure red object in OpenCV vs PIL.
questions.relatedConcept: Channel ordering convention differences between image libraries
questions.codeSnippet:
img_cv = cv2.imread("photo.jpg")
raw_pixels = img_cv[10, 5, 1]  # Green channel value at (10,5)
questions.interviewTip: Tests if the candidate encounters real-world integration bugs when bridging disparate CV pipelines.

questions.question: [Computer Vision • Test 1 • Q2] What is the mathematical effect of a 1-pixel dilation followed by a 1-pixel erosion versus a 1-pixel erosion followed by a 1-pixel dilation on a binary image?
options: Erosion followed by dilation (Closing) removes noise, while dilation followed by erosion (Opening) thins structures.
Both sequences produce identical results due to the commutative property of morphological operators.
Dilation followed by erosion (Opening) connects nearby regions and smooths boundaries, while erosion followed by dilation (Closing) fills small holes and breaks thin connections.
